persona.name: The Wellness Optimizer
persona.description: Tracks sleep, supplements, and workouts. Treats her body like a system to optimize. Willing to pay premiums for evidence-backed products.

persona.name: The Fitness Enthusiast
persona.description: Works out 4+ times a week, follows fitness creators, buys performance apparel and supplements. Brand-loyal to things that perform. Identity-adjacent purchasing.

persona.name: The Pet Parent
persona.description: Treats their pet as a family member. Reads ingredient labels on pet food. Will pay a premium for health and quality. Often owns multiple pets.

persona.name: The Busy Parent
persona.description: Dual-income household with kids. Time-poor, convenience-motivated. Buys in bulk, loves subscriptions, trusts brands that have been recommended by other parents.

persona.name: The Gen Z Aesthete
persona.description: Highly visual, identity-expressive buyer. Discovers through TikTok and Instagram. Cares about brand voice, packaging, and whether the brand stands for something.

persona.name: The Affluent Classic
persona.description: Established career or retired, disposable income, values quality and longevity over trends. Shops less frequently but at higher AOVs. Loyal to brands she trusts.

persona.name: The Sustainability Buyer
persona.description: Makes purchase decisions based on environmental and ethical footprint. Researches supply chains. Will pay more for genuinely sustainable options and is skeptical of greenwashing.

persona.name: The Convenience-First Millennial
persona.description: Urban, mid-to-high income, values speed and frictionlessness. Default to what's easy. Heavy subscription user. Low brand loyalty if another option is just as convenient.

persona.name: The Value-Conscious Shopper
persona.description: Budget-aware but not low-end. Looks for deals, reads reviews, comparison shops. Responds well to bundles, first-order discounts, and clear value articulation.

persona.name: The Gifter
persona.description: Not a persistent persona so much as a mode: any shopper within 30 days of a gifting holiday or life event. Higher AOV, looking for 'impressive-looking' purchases. Very responsive to gift-wrap and gifting messaging.

publisher.name: Studiogrid
publisher.notes: Appointment-based booking. Users are actively spending on self-care and fitness.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Wellness Optimizer, The Fitness Enthusiast

publishers.rationale: Studiogrid's audience is actively investing in self-care and spa services, making them a natural demographic for premium physical self-care products.
publishers.concern: Because users visit the platform primarily to book appointments, they may require post-booking retargeting to convert on product sales.

publisher.name: Daily Form
publisher.notes: Science-forward wellness. Audience skeptical of unsubstantiated health claims.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Wellness Optimizer, The Fitness Enthusiast

publishers.rationale: This audience is highly analytical and skeptical of unsubstantiated claims, which presents a significant barrier given the currently vague description of your health products.
publishers.concern: Your campaign risks low conversion or negative reception if you cannot back up health claims with clear scientific evidence.

publisher.name: Movewell
publisher.notes: Fitness-engaged shoppers. Strong crossover with wellness and beauty.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Wellness Optimizer, The Fitness Enthusiast

publishers.rationale: The audience has a strong demonstrated crossover interest in wellness and beauty, which creates a receptive environment for self-care products despite this being an apparel platform.
publishers.concern: Users are primarily visiting to shop for fitness apparel, meaning health and supplement ads must be highly eye-catching.

publisher.name: Pantrygood
publisher.notes: Values-driven shoppers. Responsive to clean-ingredient, sustainability, and wellness claims.

publishers.rationale: This highly health-conscious audience of grocery shoppers is exceptionally responsive to clean-ingredient and wellness claims, creating an ideal market for vitamins and supplements.
publishers.concern: These buyers expect absolute transparency regarding ingredients and sourcing.

publisher.name: Cloudfoot
publisher.notes: Tech-adjacent urban professionals. Comfort + sustainability messaging.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Wellness Optimizer, The Fitness Enthusiast

publishers.rationale: The audience consists of tech-adjacent urban professionals seeking footwear and sustainability, which does not align closely with supplements or self-care products.
publishers.concern: The focus on urban utility and shoe comfort leaves little room for engaging with general wellness messaging.
publishers.exclusionReason: The focus on urban utility and shoe comfort leaves little room for engaging with general wellness messaging.

plan.reviewNote: Given the broad nature of the current advertiser brief, we have prioritized audiences that actively spend on self-care and natural wellness while de-prioritizing platforms whose users demand rigorous clinical and scientific validation.

creatives.whyThisPersona: This persona actively tracks her health markers and wants transparent, premium supplements to optimize her physical systems. She represents a highly motivated buyer who invests in feeling her best.
creatives.headline: Optimize Your Daily Well-Being
creatives.body: Support your body's systems with premium wellness essentials designed to help you feel your best every single day.

creatives.whyThisPersona: Fitness enthusiasts demand products that help them recover quickly from training. Our wellness products directly target their desire to feel better after physical exertion.
creatives.headline: Feel Better after Every Workout
creatives.body: Keep your body performing at its peak. Our premium wellness products support active recovery so you can feel better faster.

bidding.rationale: Start on CPM bids for 14 days to buy reach and collect conversion data (there is no history yet), then switch to a target CPA once each publisher has ~30 conversions.

creativeRotation.strategy: Even rotation for 14 days, then shift weight to the best CTR per publisher.

assumptions: No budget given: assumed $10,000 for a 30-day test.
CPMs are estimated from each audience's income tier (+15% for audiences under 5M monthly impressions); real prices come from the auction.
No price given: used the spend-weighted publisher AOV (~$47) as order value.
One-time purchase: target CPA = 30% of order value as a margin-safe default.
No publisher gets more than 25% of its monthly impressions, so no single audience is saturated.
Assumed the business sells wellness-focused physical products like vitamins, supplements, or self-care items based on the phrase 'feel better'.
Assumed a typical DTC consumer target with no specific age or gender skew.

output.understanding: The advertiser offers health, physical recovery, or wellness solutions designed to help consumers improve their physical and mental well-being.

publishers.rationale: Daily Form targets science-forward wellness consumers seeking supplements and vitamins that directly help them feel better physically, matching the core brand promise.
Studiogrid users actively invest in wellness services, yoga, fitness classes, and spa treatments, aligning perfectly with physical self-care and feeling better.
Pop & Sip caters to health-curious buyers looking for functional beverages and gut health solutions that deliver a daily wellness boost.

excluded.reason: Swiftcart focuses on quick-delivery convenience and impulse purchases rather than targeted health and wellness.
Movewell is primarily activewear apparel; we prefer to prioritize direct wellness services and products.
Marlowe & Co. caters to professional and mid-life casual fashion rather than health and wellness.
Linden Park is focused on high-end classic apparel for older women, which does not fit a broad wellness value proposition.
Everbody focuses on inclusive-sized apparel and intimates rather than systemic health or wellness.
Pawline focuses on pet wellness rather than human wellness.
Pantrygood is organic groceries; while healthy, it is less directly focused on active self-care than our selected wellness channels.
Ruffco is a pet-focused retailer with no alignment to human physical recovery or wellness.
Heartfoot is a basic apparel and gifting platform, not aligned with daily feel-good wellness routines.
Northbed focuses on premium home bedding and textiles rather than direct physical health optimization.
Velvetline is specialized in Gen Z minimalist skincare and cosmetics, which is beauty-focused rather than general wellness.
Hearthstone Goods is centered around kitchen and non-toxic cookware, which is too indirect for a wellness campaign.
Kitchenly focus is meal kits and household dinner convenience rather than targeted health products.
Stride & Stem is focused on sustainable professional shoes rather than systemic physical wellbeing.
Cloudfoot is focused on footwear and activewear comfort rather than daily wellness and wellness rituals.
Tailcrate is tailored entirely to dog toys and treats.
Strandlab is personalized hair care, which is too narrow for a general 'feel better' wellness positioning.
